newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland to sell two large steel mills in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Poland to sell two large steel mills in 1997.

text.p: The treasury ministry plans to sell Poland's two largest steel mills, Huta Sedzimira and Huta Katowice SA to foreign investors, most likely next year, deputy treasury minister Wielsaw Kaczmarek said on Monday.
"Talks on selling Sedzimir and Katowice are quite well advanced... We are in talks with the world's leading companies," Kaczmarek told a news briefing.

"The whole cabinet will have to approve the privatisations ...because the two companies have strategic significance for our steel sector," he said, adding the sale was likely to take place in the second half of the year.
He said investors would be offered new shares in the two mills and initially would be allowed to hold only minority stakes in them.
"After investment promises are fulfilled the stakes could be extended to majority holdings," he said.

Investors would buy stakes in companies directly controlling steel production units in the two mills, he said. The mills' other operations would be carried out by subsidiary firms due to be carved out.
